title: Free to serve (Galatians 5:1, 13–15)
hook: stand fast in liberty, and by love serve one another
tomorrow: what do you do when doing good stops feeling worth it?

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was adoption, and the line: no longer a slave. So what does a free person do with a free day? Paul answers with something heavy and wooden.

A backpack strap that leaves a mark on your shoulder by the end of the day. Now make it wood. A yoke is a heavy bar laid across a neck, so an animal pulls wherever someone else decides. Paul reaches for that object: "Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage." Shrug it off. Stand up straight. It sounds like the last word on the subject. A few lines later, Paul sets something back on your shoulders.
screen: `A STRAP THAT LEAVES A MARK.` → `THE YOKE OF BONDAGE.` → `STAND FAST.`

segments.voice: Here it is: "For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another." Called to freedom, then told to serve. Here's the one to tell a friend: the verb Paul uses for serve comes from the same word family as his word for slave. He's being bold on purpose. Free people, he says, take up a servant's work again, but the reason has changed. Under the yoke you serve because you're owned and afraid. In love you serve because you're free and you want to. Same hands, different weight. Then Paul shrinks everything to one sentence: "For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself." He's quoting Leviticus, from the Torah. The command was there all along, and Paul holds it up as the center. Then a warning with teeth, literally: "But if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another." A community that spends its freedom on fighting eats itself. So freedom, for Paul, has a direction. Not freedom from other people. Freedom for them.
screen: `CALLED UNTO LIBERTY.` · `SERVE: A SLAVE'S VERB, BY LOVE.` · `ONE WORD: LOVE YOUR NEIGHBOR.` · `BITE AND DEVOUR, AND BE CONSUMED.` · then, large: `FREE TO SERVE.`

segments.voice: Sit with your hands open, palms up on your knees: nothing held, nothing gripped. Let your shoulders drop, as if a yoke had just been lifted off. Then, still open-handed, let one person come to mind whom these hands could serve this week, gladly, because they're free to.
Free to serve. Paul's freedom with a direction: out from under the yoke, and toward other people, by love.
The line to keep: free to serve, by love and not by fear. Go gently.
